body_md:
**item.owner_id is a foreign key without an index, filtered on by 2 endpoint(s)**

L4 · functional validation: measured faster in an offline sandbox, and the test suite shows no regression

### What was found
- Code reads item by owner_id (backend/app/api/routes/items.py:32 read_items, backend/app/api/routes/users.py:228 delete_user; inferred from the code, not observed): without an index every such lookup scans the whole table (~200000 rows now, from the database's statistics), so its cost grows with all rows, not the ones it needs. Endpoints: DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id}, GET /api/v1/items/. Cost of the index: about 3.6 MB for 200000 rows (13% of the table's 27.4 MB); every INSERT into item, UPDATE of owner_id and DELETE also writes it.
- How: the database schema was read live (read-only) and compared with the endpoints that read `item`; no one pointed at this table.

### Claim
- request_ms: 22.101 → 5.582 ms (session median) (lower is better, +75%, p = 0.029); ≥ 20% faster, permutation p < 0.05, A/A within ±10%, confirmed in new sessions: met

### What was measured
- GET /api/v1/items/: session medians 18.32 -> 5.88 ms (+68% faster), permutation p = 0.0286 (slower: 1), 95% interval of the effect [+57%, +78%]
- mechanism observed: 2048-2048 scans of an index on item.owner_id per candidate session (needed: 20)
- A/A control: +4% between two sets of base sessions
- confirmation: session medians 22.10 -> 5.58 ms (+75% faster), permutation p = 0.0286 (slower: 1), 95% interval of the effect [+62%, +80%]
- the same 20 responses on both sides, in every session, up to one correspondence per session of the ids and times the application generated
- 8 sessions alternating base and candidate, 80 measured requests on the base side after a warm-up; each session in its own sandbox with a fresh database.
- Criteria `perf-v4`, fixed before measuring: every measured call succeeds and returns the same result on both sides (canonical JSON digest); A/A: 2 base sessions against 2 more, |effect| below 10%; 4 new sessions per arm in a new order, improved again at alpha 0.05 / (candidates confirmed at this commit); at least 20% faster.
- Test suite, 3 rounds per side: base failed in 0, candidate failed in 0.
- Candidate written by: Muse Spark (Meta Model API), on this public repository's code. The workload (synthetic data and the request) was written by a model under the same routing and is kept with the experiment (sha256 `0ec9f106288d`).

### Caveats
- {'item': 200000}, measured in a sandbox; production effect not yet observed
- measured on postgres, the running system's engine
- the project's tests on both sides: the whole job
